svg.title: Fig 8 — Multi-layer columns: feeding, crossing, restocking
svg.desc: A: section of one column at the front: at rest on the flush dosing disc, the pocket at LOAD taking the bottom vial, and back at rest with the stack one layer lower. B: crossing the front position over the flush disc versus the rejected v2.0 slot. C: top view showing the pocket resting outside the turret. D: restocking through a hatch one column wide.
svg.text: Fig 8 — Multi-layer columns: feeding, crossing, restocking
Each column is a gravity-fed stack of up to 5 vials over the fixed floor; only the column at the front can drop into the dosing-disc pocket, and only the column under the hatch can be restocked.

g.text: ONE COLUMN AT THE FRONT — SECTION AT R55
The pocket replaces the slot: it is under the column only at LOAD; at REST the floor is continuous.
continuous floor: no dip, no climb
crossing drag stays at the 79 mN·m
The flush disc top gives columns a continuous floor at the front, so crossing costs nothing extra.
WHY THE POCKET RESTS OUTSIDE THE TURRET
outside the column ring and the turret
footprint: no column ever passes over
under column k only while the turret
is stopped and S1 is holding
1 S1 turns the turret — disc at REST
The pocket can only receive a vial at LOAD, and the turret never moves while it is there.
RESTOCK THROUGH THE HATCH — TOP VIEW
GOTO j → UNLOCK → load from the top,
one column wide, above the front
column j — the only one exposed
brought under the hatch by GOTO j
Only the column rotated under the hatch can be reached; the cover is solid over the rest.
